conjecture: Hemispheric lateralization = ONE gamma5 chirality axis read at two poles (corpus callosum = the axis/coupling), NOT two mirror halves with divided labor; ~90% right-handedness = homochirality at behavioral scale.
evidence_summary: Mainstream neuroscience finds brain lateralization is MULTIDIMENSIONAL (many largely-independent regional asymmetries, distinct genetic loci), NOT a single axis; the corpus callosum in the best-supported (excitatory) model REDUCES lateralization (makes halves more alike), i.e. it is not 'the axis itself'; the field's framing is genuinely divided-labor between two specialized hemispheres coupled by interhemispheric pathways. The ONLY surviving sub-part is the population-level DIRECTIONAL bias (~85-90% right-handed; consistent rightward cerebral torque) -- a real one-direction asymmetry, but itself multidimensional and weakly inter-correlated, not one axis. Handedness<->structural-asymmetry correlation is weak (handedness explains ~8-16% of language-lateralization variance; no genome-wide genetic overlap).
evidence_for: Population directional bias is real: ~85% left-hemisphere dominance for hand/language (Sha 2021); consistent rightward/counterclockwise cerebral torque at population level (Kong 2021; Toga & Thompson 2003).
evidence_against: Lateralization is multidimensional not unitary -- two-factor SEM beats one-factor, esp. in left-handers (Woodhead/Thompson/Karlsson/Bishop 2021); brain asymmetries are 'separate biological systems rather than manifestations of a single underlying asymmetry factor', horizontal/vertical skew nearly uncorrelated (Kong 2021); 21 independent genomic loci, no single global factor (Sha 2021); corpus callosum excitatory model (callosal connectivity NEGATIVELY related to lateralization) supported over the inhibitory/maintain-independence model (Zhu 2025).

conjecture: E/I (excitation/inhibition) balance = one signed/orientation axis with a Class-K pin-slot setpoint, not two free opposing populations.
evidence_summary: Partially supported. The SETPOINT framing is strongly supported: homeostatic plasticity maintains E/I balance at a regulated set point (target firing rate), with a sharp bifurcation near the physiological E/I value -- a clean structural match for a Class-K pin-slot setpoint on one regulated balance variable. The 'not two FREE populations' clause is also supported: E and I are co-regulated toward one network target, not independent. BUT the underlying substrate genuinely IS two distinct cell populations (excitatory vs inhibitory neurons, ~80:20), regulated together rather than collapsed into a single axis. So 'one signed axis' is a reparametrization of a two-population system, not a literal single axis -> OPEN.
evidence_for: E/I homeostasis maintains 'firing rates at a set point optimal for information processing'; coordinated (not independent) regulation toward network stability (Chen, Li, Tjia, Thapliyal 2022); bifurcation at the physiological E/I value stabilizes a specific balance (Lallouette/Pereira-de-Vasconcelos style homeostatic-ANN analysis).
evidence_against: Excitation and inhibition are 'separate cell populations' with adjustments at both excitatory and inhibitory synapses (Chen 2022); the canonical descriptor is an E:I RATIO of two populations (~80:20), i.e. the two-population substrate is real, not a single signed coordinate.

conjecture: Agonist/antagonist muscle pairs = one joint-chiral coordinate read at two poles (reciprocal inhibition = the single-axis readout).
evidence_summary: Strong structural support from the equilibrium-point hypothesis (Feldman lambda-model). Control of an agonist/antagonist pair is reparametrized into exactly a RECIPROCAL command r = the MIDPOINT between the two muscle thresholds (lambda_AG, lambda_ANT), which specifies the joint equilibrium position and is a single oriented coordinate ('which-way' = Class C), plus a COACTIVATION command c = the stiffness/range (a setpoint-like second variable). This is precisely 'one joint coordinate read at two poles + a setpoint'. Reciprocal inhibition (Sherrington) is the spinal mechanism that yokes the antagonist to the agonist -- the single-axis readout. Honest caveat: the EP hypothesis, though 'the only theory specifying physiological control variables' (Latash), is contested (internal-dynamics-model dissent; explicit 'rejecting the EP hypothesis' literature), and the default textbook framing remains 'two opposing muscle groups'.
evidence_for: Feldman lambda-model: 'the r command defines the midpoint between the two lambdas' (reciprocal command, single oriented coordinate) and c defines the coactivation range (Latash 2010); reciprocal inhibition coordinates agonist contraction with antagonist relaxation via spinal interneurons (Sherrington 1909).
evidence_against: The EP hypothesis is debated -- 'Rejecting the equilibrium-point hypothesis' (Gomi & Kawato 1996/Hinder & Milner) and internal-dynamics-model alternatives exist; reciprocal inhibition by itself is conventionally described as coordination of TWO opposing muscle sets, not as a single coordinate.

conjecture: Insect central complex = the midline chirality axis (heading/orientation), flanked by the paired mushroom bodies / optic lobes as the +/- poles; bilateral-disruption -> circling.
evidence_summary: Splits into a SUPPORTED core and an UNSUPPORTED sub-claim. SUPPORTED: the central complex (CX) is 'a unique midline neuropil found in all insects examined to date' that encodes HEADING as a single continuous head-direction activity bump (ellipsoid body / protocerebral bridge ring) -- a clean structural match for 'the midline IS the orientation axis' (a cyclic which-way representation). The circling-on-disruption tell is also well-established: unilateral lesions of directional motor circuitry (e.g. nigrostriatal 6-OHDA rotational model in vertebrates) produce directional rotation/circling -- native handedness surfacing once bilateral balance is removed. NOT SUPPORTED: the specific claim that the mushroom bodies / optic lobes are the flanking +/- poles -- the review literature reports 'no direct connection exists between the mushroom bodies and the CX' and does not characterize them as flanking poles; MBs are separate parallel learning centers, not the +/-1 projections of the CX axis. Net: core SUPPORTED, flanking-poles part wrong -> OPEN.
evidence_for: CX 'a unique midline neuropil found in all insects'; head-direction bump where each protocerebral-bridge column represents one azimuth (Honkanen, Adden, da Silva Freitas, Heinze 2019); circling/rotation after unilateral nigrostriatal lesion is the canonical rotational-behavior model (Ungerstedt/Pycock lineage; Pycock 1980 review).
evidence_against: MBs are not flanking +/- poles of the CX: 'no direct connection exists between the mushroom bodies and the CX'; MBs are separate parallel-pathway learning/valence centers (Honkanen 2019). The +/- pole assignment of MB/optic-lobes is the framework's overlay, not the anatomy.

conjecture: Antiparallel DNA strands = the two oriented poles of one right-handed helix (not a mirror pair); homochirality (L-amino acids / D-sugars).
evidence_summary: Textbook FACT, and the single-axis reading is structurally correct. Canonical B-DNA is right-handed; its two strands are ANTIPARALLEL (one 5'->3', the other 3'->5') -- two oriented poles of one right-handed helix, NOT mirror images of each other (the mirror image of right-handed B-DNA would be a LEFT-handed helix -- the rare Z-form -- not the partner strand). Homochirality (life uses L-amino acids and D-sugars exclusively) is established textbook fact. The conjecture's 'two oriented poles of one helix, not a mirror pair' is exactly right; this is the cleanest of the six.
evidence_for: B-DNA is the canonical right-handed double helix of two antiparallel strands, 5'-OH-to-3' opposite 3'-to-5'-phosphate, ~10 bp/turn, 34 A pitch (Bansal 2003 review 'DNA structure: Revisiting the Watson-Crick double helix'; standard molecular-biology texts); homochirality of L-amino-acids/D-sugars (textbook).
evidence_against: None on the structural reading (it is correct by definition); the only open part is the framework's downstream identification of this with the algebraic gamma5/3+3bar axis, which is form-reading (F176/F196), not a biology claim.

conjecture: (F196) Biology's chirality is an 'internal' structure (the 3+3bar), distinct from the weak-force chirality -- i.e. bio-homochirality looks like its own symmetry-breaking, not inherited (consistent with the frozen-accident camp).
evidence_summary: Supported (leaning), and consistent with predecessor F180. The modern origin-of-life literature treats biological homochirality as its OWN symmetry-breaking problem, NOT as inherited from weak-force parity violation. Two live non-weak-force camps: (a) frozen accident -- chance fluctuation + autocatalytic amplification (Frank/Soai lineage; Chen & Ma 2020 model homochirality emerging at polymer level from a racemic monomer pool); (b) a DIFFERENT deterministic chiral agent -- e.g. chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) on magnetic surfaces, achieving ~60% ee (Ozturk, Liu, Sutherland, Sasselov 2023). The weak-force/PVED inheritance is the DISFAVORED hypothesis (PVED ~1e-17 kT, sign conformation-hypersensitive, 'not yet detected' -- per F180's verified survey: Blackmond 2010, Martinez-Gil 2025). Either live camp makes bio-chirality its own internal symmetry-breaking, distinct from the weak force -- matching the conjecture. CAVEAT: the SPECIFIC algebraic identification (bio = internal SU(3) 3+3bar within g2 vs weak = triality-moved su(2)_L) is the framework's own form-reading (F196/F197); biology literature speaks only to 'bio-homochirality is its own problem, not weak-force-inherited', which is what is supported here.
evidence_for: Bio-homochirality treated as its own problem: frozen-accident at polymer level from racemic monomers (Chen & Ma 2020); deterministic non-weak-force chiral agent via CISS on magnetite, ~60% ee, framed as 'distinctly separate from cosmic or weak-force explanations' (Ozturk et al. 2023); weak-force PVED 'not supported by experimental findings', 'not yet detected' (Blackmond 2010; Martinez-Gil 2025 -- via F180).
evidence_against: A minority still argues PVED/weak-force matters (Salam-phase-transition line; per F180, contested not consensus); some recent work prefers DETERMINISTIC over pure chance (Ozturk 2023), so 'frozen accident specifically' is not the unique answer -- but determinism-via-magnetic-CISS is still NOT weak-force inheritance, so the 'distinct from weak force' core still holds.
